{{Short description|Equation in mathematical physics}}
{{Technical|date=January 2022}}
The '''Virbhadra-Ellis lens equation''' <ref>{{cite journal | last1=Virbhadra | first1=K. S. | last2=Ellis | first2=George F. R. | title=Schwarzschild black hole lensing | journal=Physical Review D | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=62 | issue=8 | date=2000-09-08 | issn=0556-2821 | doi=10.1103/physrevd.62.084003 | article-number=084003| arxiv=astro-ph/9904193 | bibcode=2000PhRvD..62h4003V | s2cid=15956589 }}</ref> in [[astronomy]] and [[mathematics]] relates to the [[angular position]]s of an unlensed source <math>\left(\beta\right)</math>, the image <math> \left(\theta\right)</math>, the Einstein bending angle of light <math>(\hat{\alpha})</math>, and the [[angular diameter]] [[lens (optics)|lens]]-source <math>\left(D_{ds}\right)</math> and observer-source <math>\left(D_s\right)</math> distances.

:<math>\tan \beta = \tan \theta - \frac{D_{ds}}{D_s} \left [\tan \theta + \tan \left (\hat{\alpha}-\theta\right ) \right ]</math>.

This approximate lens equation is useful for studying the [[gravitational lens]] in [[gravitational fields]] of any strength when the angular source position is small.
